answers.label: Q.1(a)
answers.finalAnswer: Anything that disturbs his balance because it stops him from getting what he wants, or anything that makes things difficult or more complicated for him.
answers.solution: To a common man, a problem is anything that disturbs his peace of mind (his 'equilibrium') because it stops him from achieving something he wants. It can also be anything that creates a difficulty for him or makes his situation more complicated.

answers.label: Q.1(b)
answers.finalAnswer: By managing our time well, respecting our elders, showing kindness to others and loving nature.
answers.solution: Many problems will disappear from our life if we manage our time well, respect our elders, show kindness to others and love and take care of nature. Good time management gives us a sense of achievement and keeps our mind busy, listening to parents makes us good human beings, kindness makes us better human beings, and caring for nature prevents natural calamities.

answers.label: Q.1(c)
answers.finalAnswer: Personal: a student cannot find his pencil; Global: the pandemic.
answers.solution:
Personal problem: a student who cannot find his pencil (or parents not allowing us to go somewhere).
Global problem: the pandemic, which the leaders of every country have to find a way to overcome.

answers.label: Q.1(d)
answers.finalAnswer: As an opportunity to test oneself, which teaches lessons of life and helps one become a better version of oneself.
answers.solution: For a person who loves to face problems, a problem is not a trouble but an opportunity to test himself. He believes such situations teach him many lessons of life and finally help him become a better version of himself.

answers.label: Q.1(e)
answers.finalAnswer: Problems are a part of everyone's life; many are of our own making and can be avoided by good habits, and the rest can be faced as opportunities to learn and grow.
answers.solution: Problems are a part of every person's life, from a student to a Prime Minister, and they differ in seriousness from person to person. Many of them are created by us and can be avoided through good habits such as managing time, respecting elders, being kind and caring for nature. The problems that remain should not be feared; like the people mentioned at the end of the passage, we can treat them as opportunities to learn and become better.

answers.label: Q.1(f)
answers.finalAnswer: (iv) Problems are not helpful at all.
answers.solution: (iv) is not true. The passage says that some people see problems as opportunities which teach them lessons of life and help them become better versions of themselves, so problems can be helpful.

answers.label: Q.1(g)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) utopian; (ii) compounds
answers.solution:
(i) Ideal: utopian ('we do not live in a utopian world').
(ii) Complicate: compounds ('compounds a situation for him').

answers.label: Q.1(h)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) absorbed in (our work); (ii) everything is hunky dory
answers.solution:
(i) Concentrate: 'absorbed in' ('When we are absorbed in our work').
(ii) There is no problem: 'everything is hunky dory'.

answers.label: Q.2(a)
answers.finalAnswer: The robes of a new-born child, blue as the wing of a bluebird.
answers.solution: In the early morning the weavers weave the robes of a new-born child, blue like the wing of a wild bluebird.

answers.label: Q.2(b)
answers.finalAnswer: marriage veil of a queen (coloured like the plumes of a peacock)
answers.solution: The marriage veil of a queen is purple and green coloured. The weavers weave it at nightfall, in colours 'Like the plumes of a peacock, purple or green'.

answers.label: Q.2(c)
answers.finalAnswer: The weavers.
answers.solution: The poet addresses the weavers ('Weavers, weaving at break of day').

answers.label: Q.2(d)
answers.finalAnswer: The weavers, solemn and still, weave a dead man's funeral shroud.
answers.solution: In the chilly moonlight the weavers sit solemn and still and weave a white funeral shroud for a dead man.

answers.label: Q.2(e)
answers.finalAnswer: birth, marriage (youth) and death
answers.solution: The three stages of life are birth (the robe of a new-born child), marriage or youth (the marriage veil of a queen) and death (the funeral shroud).

answers.label: Q.3
answers.solution:
25, Rajpur Road
Dehradun

15 June 2021

The Editor
The Times of India
New Delhi

Subject: Preparing for a future pandemic

Sir,

Through your newspaper, I wish to suggest how our nation can face another pandemic in the future.

First, every district must have a well-equipped hospital with enough beds, oxygen and trained staff, so that we are not caught unprepared again. Second, the government should keep a stock of medicines, masks and vaccines. Third, people must form healthy habits such as washing hands, wearing masks in crowded places and eating nutritious food.

Schools should be ready with online classes, so that children's education does not stop. Citizens must also stop spreading rumours and follow only official information. Lastly, neighbours should help the elderly and the poor during lockdowns.

If the government and the people work together, we can face any pandemic bravely.

Yours faithfully,
Arjun Sharma

answers.label: Q.4
answers.solution:
Title: Kinds of Students

Students are generally good, naughty or weak. Good students are intelligent, obedient, punctual and modest. Naughty students, though often intelligent, disturb the class, quarrel and even steal. Weak students do poorly in exams because they cannot follow lessons, owing to a poor foundation or a lack of confidence, motivation or guidance. Teachers and parents should together find the cause, motivate such students, clear their doubts and help them set realistic goals.

(About 70 words, roughly one-third of the original.)

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
My Favourite Dream

I dream I wear an olive green,
The proudest cadet ever seen;
I march along with head held high,
Beneath the bright and open sky.

I dream I fly a fighter plane,
Above the hills, the clouds, the rain;
The rivers shine like silver thread,
The mountains stand with snowy head.

I dream I guard our border land,
With brave companions close at hand;
Through winter cold and summer heat,
Our hearts stay strong and know no defeat.

I wake and find it is the dawn,
My lovely dream is not yet gone;
I'll study hard and work each day,
To make my dream come true one day.

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
Effect of the Pandemic on the Education of School-Going Children
By Arjun Sharma, Class VII

In March 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic shut the gates of schools across India. For more than a year, crores of children studied at home. This sudden change affected their education in many ways.

The biggest change was the move to online classes. Children who had smartphones, computers and good internet could continue learning. Teachers learnt new skills, and students became familiar with technology. However, many poor children had no device, or one phone shared by three brothers and sisters. In villages, the internet was weak. These children fell far behind.

Learning also suffered in other ways. It is hard to concentrate in front of a screen for hours, and many students lost interest. Practical subjects such as science experiments, sports, music and art could hardly be taught online. Examinations were cancelled or held from home, so many students did not work seriously. Some children, especially girls, left school altogether to help their families.

The pandemic hurt children's minds too. Without friends, games and the school routine, many felt lonely and anxious. Long hours on screens caused eye strain and headaches.

Yet there were some good results. Children learnt to study on their own, to use technology and to value school and friends more than ever.

Now that schools have reopened, teachers and parents must help children make up for the lost learning through extra classes and patient support. The government should provide devices and internet to poor students, so that no child is left behind if such a situation ever comes again.

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
Title: My Best Friend, Bruno

Riya was eight when her father brought home a little golden puppy. She named him Bruno, and from that day they were never apart.

Every evening Riya and Bruno walked down the long path through the forest near their house. One autumn evening, a strong wind blew and Riya slipped on the wet leaves and twisted her ankle. She could not stand up, and it was getting dark.

Bruno barked loudly and ran all the way home. He pulled at her mother's dupatta until she followed him. Soon Riya's parents found her and carried her home.

From then on, whenever Riya walked down that path, she kept one hand on Bruno's soft back. A dog is truly a faithful friend.

(About 120 words.)

answers.label: Q.8
answers.finalAnswer: (a) He refused to accept the award with dignity.; (b) Having scored the highest runs in the match, he was adjudged man of the match.; (c) He is so young that he cannot understand the situation.; (d) He was late but he was not punished.; (e) Jaipur is more beautiful than most other cities in India.; (f) The two girls proposed that the show should begin.; (g) My mother said to them, "I have not received his letter."; (h) no passive possible ('come' is intransitive); (i) Let them give each student a pen after the assembly.; (j) He followed his advice unhesitatingly.
answers.solution:
(a) He refused to accept the award with dignity.
(b) Having scored the highest runs in the match, he was adjudged man of the match.
(c) He is so young that he cannot understand the situation.
(d) He was late but he was not punished.
(e) Jaipur is more beautiful than most other cities in India.
(f) The two girls proposed that the show should begin. ('Let' showing a proposal becomes 'proposed that ... should'.)
(g) My mother said to them, "I have not received his letter." ('My letter' in the reported speech is the speaker's child's letter, so the mother would say 'his letter' or 'my son's letter'.)
(h) This sentence cannot be changed into the passive voice. 'Come' is an intransitive verb (it has no object), and only a verb with an object has a passive form. As printed, this part is defective; the sentence stays: Why didn't they come home yesterday?
(i) Let them give each student a pen after the assembly.
(j) He followed his advice unhesitatingly (or readily).

answers.label: Q.9
answers.finalAnswer: GARDEN; DANGER; DRAGON; ORANGE; MODERN
answers.solution:
Five words from the letters of ARMAGEDON, each of at least four letters with no letter repeated:
1. GARDEN: We grow roses in our garden.
2. DANGER: The soldiers were not afraid of danger.
3. DRAGON: The story was about a dragon that guarded a treasure.
4. ORANGE: I eat an orange every morning.
5. MODERN: Our school has a modern computer lab.

answers.label: Q.10
answers.finalAnswer: (a) He that would eat the fruit must climb the tree.; (b) Should he come home in time, I will be very happy.; (c) Walk carefully lest you should fall.; (d) My brother came home after I had finished the work.; (e) Only when I read the newspaper did I know that he won the match.; (f) Before the advent of the internet, we wrote letters by hand.; (g) We waited eagerly for the postman to deliver one.; (h) The television serials of those days were epic drama.; (i) Television then meant just one channel.; (j) Video and cassette recorders were still in vogue.
answers.solution:
(a) He that would eat the fruit must climb the tree.
(b) Should he come home in time, I will be very happy.
(c) Walk carefully lest you should fall.
(d) My brother came home after I had finished the work.
(e) Only when I read the newspaper did I know that he won the match.
(f) Before the advent of the internet, we wrote letters by hand.
(g) We waited eagerly for the postman to deliver one.
(h) The television serials of those days were epic drama.
(i) Television then meant just one channel.
(j) Video and cassette recorders were still in vogue.

Note: the jumble in (e) is misprinted. It prints 'know' twice and 'I' only once, while the sentence needs 'I' twice and 'know' once; the answer uses the sensible reading.

answers.finalAnswer: (a) rigorous; (b) uncontrollably wild; (c) to strive or excel; (d) puzzling; (e) rise and float in air
answers.solution:
(a) AUSTERE: (ii) rigorous (strict and severe).
(b) BERSERK: (iv) uncontrollably wild.
(c) EMULATE: (i) to strive to equal or excel (printed 'to strive or excel'). To emulate someone is to try to match or do better than him, usually by copying his example.

answers.label: Q.13
answers.finalAnswer: (a) a bad egg / put all your eggs in one basket; (b) pull someone's leg / not have a leg to stand on; (c) kill two birds with one stone / a bird's eye view; (d) see eye to eye / turn a blind eye; (e) Achilles' heel / take to one's heels
answers.solution:
(a) Egg: a bad egg (a dishonest person); put all your eggs in one basket (risk everything on one plan).
(b) Leg: pull someone's leg (tease someone); not have a leg to stand on (have no support for one's argument).
(c) Bird: kill two birds with one stone (do two things with one action); a bird's eye view (a view from high above).
(d) Eyes: see eye to eye (agree fully); turn a blind eye (pretend not to notice).
(e) Heel: Achilles' heel (a weak point); take to one's heels (run away).

answers.label: Q.15
answers.finalAnswer: (a) are; (b) is; (c) has; (d) was; (e) are; (f) are; (g) likes; (h) were; (i) are; (j) is
answers.solution:
(a) A number of people are going to attend the function. ('A number of' means many, so plural.)
(b) Dal and rice is my favourite dish. (Together they make one dish.)
(c) Most of the sugar has been sold. ('Sugar' is uncountable.)
(d) Half of his income was spent on construction of his house. ('Income' is singular.)
(e) The police are trying to catch the thief. ('Police' always takes a plural verb.)
(f) Neither Rohan nor the two students are coming today. (The verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students'.)
(g) One of the boys likes to watch horror movies. (The subject is 'one'.)
(h) If I were the prime minister, I would help the poor. (An imaginary condition takes 'were'.)
(i) Anil and Arun are playing in the park.
(j) Aman as well as his friends is coming over for a party. (The verb agrees with the first subject, 'Aman'.)
